prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins rather than inhibit them

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation meets the standard I keep returning to: it is completely new and it has already had real consequences. PROTACs turn a cellular process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into a designable chemical reaction by bringing a ligase and a target together with a small molecule. Molecular glues, explained by the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs, show that the same principle was operating in an old clinical puzzle. The idea is modular and general, it reaches targets that were considered undruggable, and it has been reproduced across hundreds of laboratories with several degraders in late-stage trials. Attribution can be made precise with three names: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. That combination covers both the heterobifunctional and the monovalent branches of the field.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug has yet been approved, so the therapeutic proof is still pending and the committee could reasonably wait. The three-person limit also forces a hard exclusion: Ciulli's VHL ligands and structure-guided ternary-complex design, and the work of Gray, Sakamoto and Kim, are decisive for how the field works today, and Ito is inseparable from Handa on cereblon. Sakamoto was a co-author of the original 2001 report. A prize that leaves these people out risks looking like an arbitrary cut of a field that is still moving quickly. Finally, much of the visible success is pharmacology, so we must be sure that the prize is for the chemical principle and not for the drugs.

responses.point: Peter ranks PROTACs only fourth, because no approved PROTAC drug exists and long-term impact is not yet established, and he also doubts that the attribution gives a clean three-person set.
responses.response: I take the prematurity point seriously, but I think approval is the wrong test for a chemistry prize. The principle is already established by independent replication, by structural work on ternary complexes, and by the approved lenalidomide-class glues, whose mechanism is exactly the cereblon story. Peter's own preferred candidate shows why I am less worried: Gray and Winkler's electron-tunnelling work was recognised as fundamental long after the physics was settled, but it has not changed what chemists do in the way degraders have in the last decade. I agree the attribution is the real difficulty, which is why I propose Crews, Deshaies and Handa and not a wider set. I would be more hesitant about nitrogenase, where he notes the mechanism of N2 binding and the catalytic intermediates is unsettled.

responses.point: Heiner, our chair, ranks sequencing by synthesis first as an overdue chemistry-driven invention with enormous consequences, and judges PROTACs somewhat early on the therapeutic side.
responses.response: I agree that the consequences of Solexa chemistry are enormous and that Balasubramanian and Klenerman are the clear chemical core. My reservation is the one I recorded in my own ballot: next-generation sequencing was built by several lineages (Solexa, 454, and others), and a prize for the Solexa pair alone, which leaves out Rothberg and Mayer, may look incomplete. The prize also has an uncomfortable overlap with the territory of the 1980 Sanger prize and sits close to Physiology or Medicine. I would not block it, but I rank it below degraders because the originality of the chemical idea in B026 is, to my mind, greater and the attribution cleaner. I accept his point that approval of a first PROTAC would strengthen the case, and I am willing to let that timing argument carry weight.

responses.point: Andrei ranks base editing fourth and would credit David R. Liu alone, treating Komor and Gaudelli as lead researchers in his laboratory and noting that timing is early.
responses.response: I rank base editing second and I disagree on one point: Komor's cytosine base editor and Gaudelli's adenine base editor were distinct inventions, and the adenine editor needed a deaminase to be evolved to act on DNA, which does not exist in nature. That is real chemistry and real protein engineering and not only direction of a laboratory. I would however accept a Liu-only configuration if the committee prefers it, because the Target-AID work of Nishida and Kondo makes the credit for the category contestable. I share his concern that the field is young. That is why base editing is my first alternative and not my preferred configuration: the 2020 prize for CRISPR makes the follow-on question fair.

responses.point: Emma ranks phase separation first as a general physical-chemical principle of intracellular organisation, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the credited trio.
responses.response: The idea is important, and I welcome a physical-chemistry argument at the top of a chemistry list. My concern is maturity: whether the cellular condensates described are truly liquid-liquid phase separated in vivo, and how much of it is quantitative, is still debated, and Pappu and Mittag's sequence-encoded theory would be left out of a three-person prize. I hold phase separation to my game-changer standard of consequences that are demonstrated, and I do not think it meets that standard yet. That is the reason I did not place it on my own ballot. I would like to hear which of the in-cell claims she regards as firm enough to cite.

responses.point: Daniel shares first place for degraders with the same trio, but notes that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are decisive and that the choice is hard.
responses.response: We agree on the trio, and I think we should be honest that this is a choice between contributions of equal standing. Ciulli's structure-guided work made PROTACs into drugs by showing how a ternary complex is built, and Deshaies' role is more in the early concept and in the cullin-RING ligase biochemistry. My reading is that the concept and the mechanistic discovery take priority over the later optimisation, which is why I keep Deshaies and Handa. I would be willing to hear a case for Ciulli replacing Deshaies, in line with Zou Xiaodong's trio that substitutes him, if someone can show that the early proof of concept was less decisive than I believe.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli should displace Deshaies, or whether Sakamoto and Ito should be considered, is not resolved.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the first approved PROTAC drug before recognising the field.
My ballot recollection of clinical status and trial stage is from memory and is not verified.
Whether base editing, which follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, would be seen as too early or a natural follow-on.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates: my connections are Arieh Warshel (empirical valence bond collaboration), the Uppsala structural biology and ribosome community, and my committee colleagues, and none of these appear among the credited names on the shortlist.
